problem.headline:
You answer for care
you cannot verify
problem.sub: Custody carries the responsibility. The healthcare vendor holds the data. Too often, no one is positioned to connect the two, so problems surface late and leadership can't independently verify the care being delivered.
problem.lead: Sound familiar? Challenges we hear from custody and health leaders, and how independent quality oversight helps.

items.title: Performance measured only from the inside
items.text: Every vendor should run its own QA and CQI program, and we support that. We add an unbiased, expert review that measures performance against NCCHC standards and applicable state and contract requirements.

items.title: Consultants who don't know jails
items.text: Custody and clinical care delivery (medical and behavioral health) have to work in lock-step. Our recommendations meet standards and requirements without creating barriers between them.

items.title: Reports that sit on a shelf
items.text: We stay through the corrective action: clear owners, due dates, and follow-up review to confirm compliance is sustained and improvement continues.

items.title: Compliance tracked in spreadsheets
items.text: We make clear what's measured and how, so the data is transparent and translated into terms custody, clinical teams, and leadership all understand.

items.title: Surprises you hear about last
items.text: Regular review and early reporting shift the culture from reactive to proactive. Leadership hears about issues first, with a plan already attached.

problem.transition: Independent quality oversight closes that gap.

services.headline:
Independent support at every
stage of your healthcare contract
services.sub: From writing the RFP to verifying the monthly numbers, each engagement is scoped and deliverable-based, and led by an experienced practitioner.

items.title: Quality Oversight (QA + CQI)
items.text: Ongoing independent review of contracted health services, combining record review, onsite observation, corrective action tracking and ongoing vendor performance review.

items.title: Behavioral Health Quality Oversight
items.text: The same QA and CQI model applied to mental health and substance use care, including suicide prevention and medication treatment continuity.

items.title: Risk Management & Compliance Review
items.text: Review against contracts, policies, NCCHC standards, state regulatory requirements and consent decrees, including mortality and critical-incident review.

items.title: NCCHC Accreditation Readiness
items.text: Gap assessments, mock surveys and standard-by-standard preparation before the surveyors arrive.

items.title: Staffing & Operational Analysis
items.text: Studies of staffing levels, hours, overtime, agency and locum use, and workflow throughput.

items.title: Care Coordination & Case Management
items.text: Design of intake, transfer, release, discharge and reentry workflows, including Medicaid enrollment, community care linkage and medication bridge supply.

items.title: Data Analytics & Custom Reporting
items.text: Analytics built on data facilities already collect, with documentation for consent decree and oversight obligations.

items.title: EHR / EMR Advisory
items.text: Guidance on correctional EHR selection, implementation, clinical champion support and go-live readiness.

items.title: RFP & Procurement Support
items.text: RFP development, performance measures, vendor cost analysis and ongoing vendor performance review, written so performance can be measured after the award.

items.title: Interim & Fractional Leadership
items.text: Experienced executives for healthcare operations, clinical programs, and quality, risk and compliance during a vacancy, transition or turnaround.

benefits.headline:
Evidence you can put in front
of your board and counsel
benefits.sub: Every engagement ends with something you can act on and something you can show.

items.title: An objective read on your vendor
items.text: Monitoring built from your own records gives an objective, verified picture of performance.

items.title: A path to NCCHC accreditation
items.text: Know where you stand against the standards and what to fix before the survey.

items.title: Stronger contracts and RFPs
items.text: Measurable requirements, clear remedies and accountable terms that hold after the award.

items.title: Documentation that holds up
items.text: Dated, sourced findings ready for litigation, consent decrees and oversight bodies.

commitments.title: What we commit to on every engagement

items.title: Scoped, deliverable-based engagements
items.text: You approve a scope and a price before work starts.

items.title: Full independence
items.text: We do not deliver care, and we take no revenue from the vendors we review.

items.title: Findings backed by data
items.text: Every finding traces to a source record, so it stands when it is challenged.

commitments.note: Accreditation and legal determinations rest with NCCHC and the courts. Our role is to prepare you, give you objective evidence, and stand behind our findings.

about.headline: Partners in quality
about.tagline: Where Accountability Meets Action in Correctional Healthcare
body: People in custody are entitled to constitutionally adequate healthcare, and the agencies responsible for them need an objective way to know whether it is being delivered. We provide independent quality oversight alongside the jail or prison and its healthcare vendor.

values.title: Independent
values.text: No care delivery, and no revenue from the vendors we review.

values.title: Credible
values.text: Findings come from surveyors, physicians and executives who have held the roles.

values.title: Collaborative
values.text: We work alongside custody staff, health staff and your vendor to fix what the data shows.

values.title: Experience
values.text: Deep California experience (CCHCS, CDCR, DMHC, DHCS, Title 15, CalAIM) and correctional healthcare work with agencies across the country.
